column1: # T-HOLES (H01 layer 1): every class of the pre-scan hole hunt (297) and of the pre-scan
# design check (21), one row each. The test tests/stack_holes.rs reads this file.
# Columns (tab-separated): name family goal path prefix open mid close suffix n_abort hunt valid expect
#   family  the hunt rule (1-18) or the design-check class (K1-K6) of an abort row; else control
#   path    compile | eval (compile_eval, direct, sloppy) | function (the body of Function) |
#   text    prefix + open x n + mid + close x n + suffix; "{i}" in open or close is the level
#           index 0..n-1. Escapes: \n \r \t \\ \u{HEX}; no raw control or format byte.
#   n_abort the smallest level count at which the hunt saw an abort; empty: only at 2,000,000
#   hunt    the hunt result: ABORT, clean, runs, rc1 (a run-time error) or timing (slow, clean)
#   valid   the text is a valid program in node 26.13.1 at n = 3 (eval, Function: the inner text)
#   expect  the allowed results, ";"-separated cases of "kind|kind" or "kind|kind@n". A case
#           without "@n" runs at the sizes of its test set; "@n" runs at exactly n (the hunt
#           size of a class that ran only near the caps). Kinds: Ok, Syntax, Unsupported,
# The table is made by a script from the generators, and each expansion was compared with the
# generator text byte for byte. Never change a row to make a test pass.
# The last 3 rows (A21-*) are not hunt classes: review R2 A2-1, eval of a TS type-name chain
# (oxc parses it in JS mode with a non-fatal error). Before the layer-2 walk gated these chains,
# each one aborted at 4,000,000 levels (debug and release). They are controls: hunt clean is
# the result with the gates, and they are written by hand (no generator).
